theory.overview: Graphs model relationships between objects using vertices (nodes) and edges. They're ubiquitous: social networks (people as vertices, friendships as edges), road networks (intersections as vertices, roads as edges), web pages (pages as vertices, links as edges). Graphs can be directed (edges have direction) or undirected, weighted (edges have weights) or unweighted. This chapter covers graph representation, traversal (BFS, DFS), and fundamental graph algorithms.

sections.title: Graph Representation
sections.content: Adjacency matrix: n×n matrix where matrix[i][j] = 1 if edge i→j exists. Space: $O(V^2)$. Good for dense graphs, O(1) edge check. Adjacency list: array of lists, each vertex has list of neighbors. Space: $O(V+E)$. Good for sparse graphs, efficient for iteration. Edge list: list of (u, v) pairs. Space: $O(E)$. Simple but inefficient for most operations.

sections.title: Graph Traversal - BFS
sections.content: Breadth-First Search explores level by level from source. Uses queue. Visits all vertices at distance k before distance k+1. Time: $O(V+E)$. Space: $O(V)$ for queue and visited. Applications: shortest path in unweighted graph, connected components, bipartite check. BFS tree has property that path from source to any vertex is shortest.
sections.algorithm: Queue = [source], visited = {source}. While queue: v = dequeue, for each neighbor u: if not visited, mark visited, enqueue u.

sections.title: Graph Traversal - DFS
sections.content: Depth-First Search explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking. Uses stack (explicit or recursion). Time: $O(V+E)$. Space: $O(V)$ for recursion stack. Applications: cycle detection, topological sort, connected components, maze solving. DFS tree has back edges (to ancestors) and cross edges.
sections.algorithm: DFS(v): mark visited, for each neighbor u: if not visited, DFS(u).

sections.title: Graph Properties
sections.content: Degree: number of edges incident to vertex. In directed: in-degree (edges to vertex), out-degree (edges from vertex). Path: sequence of vertices where consecutive vertices are adjacent. Cycle: path that starts and ends at same vertex. Connected: path exists between any two vertices. Complete: edge exists between every pair of vertices. Bipartite: vertices can be divided into two sets with no edges within each set.
properties: Cycle: path starting and ending at same vertex
Connected: path between any two vertices
Bipartite: two colorable, no odd cycles

sections.title: Graph Types
sections.content: Directed vs undirected: edges have direction or not. Weighted vs unweighted: edges have weights or not. Simple vs multigraph: no multiple edges vs allow multiple edges. Cyclic vs acyclic: contains cycles or not. Tree: connected acyclic graph. DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph): directed with no cycles. Complete graph: edge between every pair.

keyConcepts.name: Adjacency List
keyConcepts.description: Most common representation. Array of lists. Space O(V+E). Efficient for sparse graphs (most real-world graphs are sparse).
keyConcepts.advantage: Space-efficient for sparse graphs, fast neighbor iteration

keyConcepts.name: BFS Level Order
keyConcepts.description: Explores by distance from source. Queue ensures level-by-level processing. Shortest path in unweighted graphs.
keyConcepts.property: First time visiting vertex = shortest path from source

keyConcepts.name: DFS Backtracking
keyConcepts.description: Explores deep before wide. Recursion stack or explicit stack. Useful for exploring all paths, cycle detection.
keyConcepts.use: Topological sort, cycle detection, maze solving

keyConcepts.name: Visited Set
keyConcepts.description: Track visited vertices to avoid revisiting and infinite loops in cycles. Essential for both BFS and DFS.

steps.title: Initialize
steps.description: Create visited set, queue (BFS) or stack (DFS). Add source vertex.

steps.title: Process Vertex
steps.description: Dequeue (BFS) or pop (DFS) vertex. Process it (mark, record distance, etc.).

steps.title: Explore Neighbors
steps.description: For each neighbor of current vertex: if not visited, mark visited, add to queue/stack.
steps.code: for u in neighbors[v]: if u not in visited: visited.add(u); queue.append(u);

steps.title: Repeat
steps.description: Continue until queue/stack empty. All reachable vertices visited.

steps.title: Handle Disconnected
steps.description: For disconnected graphs, repeat BFS/DFS from each unvisited vertex.
steps.code: for v in vertices: if v not in visited: BFS(v);

practiceProblems.title: Number of Islands
practiceProblems.description: Count islands (connected '1's) in 2D grid using DFS/BFS.
practiceProblems.solution: Iterate all cells. When '1' found, increment count, BFS/DFS to mark all connected '1's as visited.
practiceProblems.hints: BFS/DFS from each unvisited '1', mark visited

practiceProblems.title: Clone Graph
practiceProblems.description: Deep clone a graph with node references.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS/DFS with hash map: original → clone. When visiting node, create clone if not exists, add neighbors.

practiceProblems.title: Course Schedule
practiceProblems.description: Determine if can finish all courses given prerequisites (detect cycle in DAG).
practiceProblems.solution: Topological sort using DFS (cycle detection) or BFS (Kahn's algorithm). If cycle exists, impossible.

practiceProblems.title: Course Schedule II
practiceProblems.description: Return ordering of courses to finish all (topological sort).
practiceProblems.solution: Topological sort using DFS (post-order) or BFS (Kahn's). Return order if no cycle.

practiceProblems.title: Graph Valid Tree
practiceProblems.description: Check if graph is valid tree (n nodes, n-1 edges, connected, no cycles).
practiceProblems.solution: Check n-1 edges. BFS/DFS from any node, check if all visited and no cycles (edge to visited non-parent).

practiceProblems.title: Number of Connected Components
practiceProblems.description: Count connected components in undirected graph.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS/DFS from each unvisited vertex. Count how many times we start new traversal.
practiceProblems.hints: BFS/DFS from each unvisited, count traversals

practiceProblems.title: Surrounded Regions
practiceProblems.description: Capture 'O' regions surrounded by 'X' (not on border).
practiceProblems.solution: Mark 'O's connected to border as safe (BFS/DFS from border). Convert remaining 'O' to 'X'.
practiceProblems.hints: Mark border-connected 'O' as safe, convert rest

practiceProblems.title: Rotting Oranges
practiceProblems.description: Find minutes until no fresh oranges remain (2 rots adjacent 1s).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from all initially rotten oranges. Queue stores positions. Count minutes until queue empty.
practiceProblems.hints: Multi-source BFS from all rotten oranges

practiceProblems.title: Word Ladder
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord, changing one letter at a time.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from beginWord. For each word, try all one-letter mutations. If in dict and not visited, add to queue.

practiceProblems.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
practiceProblems.description: Find cells where water can flow to both Pacific and Atlantic oceans.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS/DFS from Pacific border (left/top) and Atlantic border (right/bottom). Mark reachable cells. Intersection is answer.
practiceProblems.hints: Two BFS/DFS from oceans, find intersection

practiceProblems.title: Redundant Connection
practiceProblems.description: Find edge that can be removed to make tree (n nodes, n edges, one cycle).
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find. Add edges one by one. If edge connects already connected components, it's redundant.

practiceProblems.title: Graph Bipartite Check
practiceProblems.description: Check if graph is bipartite (can be colored with 2 colors, no adjacent same color).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS/DFS with 2-coloring. Start with color 0, neighbors get color 1. If conflict, not bipartite.

practiceProblems.title: Is Graph Bipartite
practiceProblems.description: Check if undirected graph is bipartite.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS with coloring. For each component, 2-color. If edge connects same color, not bipartite.

practiceProblems.title: Possible Bipartition
practiceProblems.description: Given dislikes between people, can we split into two groups where no one dislikes their group?
practiceProblems.solution: Graph where edge = dislike. Check if bipartite.
practiceProblems.hints: Graph with dislike edges, check bipartite

practiceProblems.title: Find Eventual Safe States
practiceProblems.description: Find nodes that eventually reach terminal node (no outgoing edges) in directed graph.
practiceProblems.solution: Reverse graph, BFS from terminal nodes. Nodes reachable in reverse graph are safe.

practiceProblems.title: Keys and Rooms
practiceProblems.description: Check if can visit all rooms starting from room 0 (each room has keys to other rooms).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS/DFS from room 0. Collect keys, visit rooms. Check if all rooms visited.

practiceProblems.title: Reorder Routes
practiceProblems.description: Minimum edges to reverse so every node can reach node 0.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from node 0. Count edges that go opposite direction of traversal.
practiceProblems.hints: BFS from node 0, count wrong-direction edges

practiceProblems.title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
practiceProblems.description: Check if path exists from source to destination in undirected graph.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS/DFS from source. Check if destination reached.

practiceProblems.title: All Paths from Source to Target
practiceProblems.description: Find all paths from source to target in DAG.
practiceProblems.solution: DFS with backtracking. Track current path. When target reached, add path to result.

practiceProblems.title: Longest Increasing Path in Matrix
practiceProblems.description: Find longest increasing path (adjacent, strictly increasing) in matrix.
practiceProblems.solution: DFS with memoization. For each cell, find longest increasing path starting there. Cache results.
practiceProblems.hints: DFS with memoization, longest from each cell

practiceProblems.title: Critical Connections
practiceProblems.description: Find critical connections (bridges) in network (edges whose removal disconnects graph).
practiceProblems.solution: Tarjan's algorithm. Track discovery time and low time. Edge is bridge if low[child] > disc[node].
practiceProblems.hints: Tarjan's algorithm, discovery and low times

practiceProblems.title: Accounts Merge
practiceProblems.description: Merge accounts with same email (each account has list of emails).
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find on emails. Accounts with same email connected. Group by root, sort emails.

practiceProblems.title: Evaluate Division
practiceProblems.description: Calculate division results from equations (a/b = 2.0, b/c = 3.0 → a/c = 6.0).
practiceProblems.solution: Build graph where edge weight = division value. BFS/DFS to find path product.
practiceProblems.hints: Graph with edge weights, BFS/DFS for path product

practiceProblems.title: Sentence Similarity II
practiceProblems.description: Check if sentences are similar given similarity pairs (transitive).
practiceProblems.solution: Build graph from similarity pairs. For each word pair, check if connected (BFS/DFS).

practiceProblems.title: Path With Minimum Effort
practiceProblems.description: Find path from top-left to bottom-right minimizing maximum height difference.
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra's variant. Min-heap by max effort. Track minimum max effort to each cell.

minigame.title: Graph Master
minigame.description: Explore graphs! BFS, DFS, and visualize traversal step by step.
